newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see World Bank all alone with Kiwi deal.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see World Bank all alone with Kiwi deal.

text.p: A New Zealand dollar offering from the World Bank was the only item of note in the primary market on Friday morning. The NZ$200 million five-year offering, carrying a 7.25 percent coupon, was lead managed by Toronto-Dominion.
A syndicate manager at TorDom said the deal was flat to the curve, as against recent EIB and KfW deals which, on Thursday, were trading around 17 and 12 basis points through respectively.
"Against that background the deal has gone superbly well. We have bought very few bonds back so far," he said, adding there had been great demand to be included in the group.
Mainstream new issues activity has long since ceased until the year-end break is over.
